title: The CEO’s Guide to Productive Tension with Your CFO
gist: BCG's CEO Insomnia Index finds 26% of CEOs see their CFO as the biggest threat to their job and CFOs top the list of executives CEOs plan to replace within six months. BCG argues the tension should be managed, not eliminated, through clear expectations, welcomed dissent, relationship investment and explicit succession planning.

insights.claim: 26% of CEOs say their CFO poses the greatest threat to their job security of any C-suite member, per BCG's CEO Insomnia Index.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: CFO turnover and CEO-CFO friction are a governance risk signal to monitor in companies under performance pressure.
insights.quote: one in four CEOs named their chief financial officer, according to The BCG CEO Insomnia Index
insights.locator: In the pressure cooker of the C-suite

insights.claim: CFOs rank first among senior executives that CEOs plan to replace, and 57% of CEOs plan leadership team changes within six months.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Expect elevated CFO turnover announcements; abrupt CFO exits can precede guidance resets or strategy changes.
insights.quote: CFOs also top the list of senior executives that CEOs plan to replace in the next six months.
insights.locator: In the pressure cooker of the C-suite

insights.claim: The CFO is a perceived threat because of direct board access and because the CFO supplies the financial evidence directors use to judge whether forecasts are realistic and transformations are delivering promised value.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: CFO commentary and departures are a credible read on how the board views management's forecasts.
insights.quote: Put simply, the CFO can strongly influence how the board perceives the CEO.

insights.claim: When CEO-CFO friction erodes trust, it undermines decision making, damages alignment with the board and limits the company's ability to grow.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Visible CEO-CFO conflict is a leading indicator of weaker capital allocation and strategy execution.

insights.claim: Tension between CEO and CFO should be managed rather than eliminated: when both trust they share goals, differences become productive dissent over key decisions and lead to better outcomes.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A CFO who challenges the CEO is a positive governance signal, while an absence of challenge may mean weak discipline.
insights.quote: The goal is not to eliminate friction, but to ensure that it strengthens decisions instead of straining the relationship.
insights.locator: What CEOs Can Do to Foster Mutual Trust

insights.claim: Move 1 is setting clear expectations: defining roles, decision rights and what success and failure look like for the CFO early, so disagreements stay about decisions rather than personalities.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Ambiguous decision rights during major strategic moves raise the risk of conflict and execution failure.

insights.claim: Move 2 is welcoming dissent: CEOs should treat CFO challenge as a stress test that strengthens plans before investors, the board and other stakeholders scrutinize them.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Plans pre-tested by a strong CFO are less likely to disappoint investors.

insights.claim: Move 3 is investing in the relationship: working around a distrusted CFO usually creates more problems over time, and visible friction between the two lets the board realize it has a problem.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: CEOs who bypass their CFO signal governance weakness that the board will eventually notice.
insights.quote: Stop thinking about the relationship as something to manage, and start thinking about something to invest in

insights.claim: As the CFO role becomes more strategic, boards increasingly see CFOs as potential CEO successors, which adds to CEO anxiety.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: CFO appointments and tenure are increasingly a CEO succession signal to watch.
insights.locator: Final Gut Check: Create a Succession Plan

insights.claim: CEOs and boards should hold an explicit succession discussion: if the CFO is not a candidate, that clarity removes uncertainty, and if so, the CEO can develop the CFO and help decide when to hand over.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Companies with transparent succession planning carry lower leadership-transition risk.
insights.locator: Final Gut Check: Create a Succession Plan

insights.claim: Modern CFOs play an increasingly strategic role and are key to driving enterprise performance, so CEOs should coach the CFO to be a forward-looking architect of enterprise value.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The CFO's growing strategic remit makes CFO quality a more important input in judging management teams.
insights.quote: Modern-day CFOs play an increasingly strategic role and are key to driving enterprise performance
insights.locator: Final Gut Check: Create a Succession Plan
